audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Jehoahaz and Jehoash reigns, Elisha's final illness, arrow oracle, death, grave revival, and Aramean recovery narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for imperial oppression, military devastation, unnamed deliverer, Elisha's fatal illness, king's grief, embodied arrow ritual, prophetic anger over ambiguous performance, grave contact and revival, covenant compassion, and three military recoveries.

verses.restored: In twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned seventeen years.

familiar.text: In the three and twentieth year of Joash the son of Ahaziah king of Judah Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned seventeen years.

modern.text: In the twenty-third year of the reign of Joash son of Ahaziah over Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria seventeen years.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן אֲחַזְיָ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָחָ֨ז בֶּן יֵה֤וּא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן שְׁבַ֥ע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH and walked after sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not turn from them.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and followed the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit; he did not turn away from them.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַ֠יֵּלֶךְ אַחַ֨ר חַטֹּ֜את יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּן נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹא סָ֥ר מִמֶּֽנָּה

verses.restored: Anger of YHWH burned against Israel, and he gave them into hand of Hazael king of Aram and into hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael all days.

familiar.text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael, all their days.

modern.text: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He delivered them continually into the hands of Hazael king of Aram and his son Ben-hadad.

original.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֞ם בְּיַ֣ד חֲזָאֵ֣ל מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֗ם וּבְיַ֛ד בֶּן הֲדַ֥ד בֶּן חֲזָאֵ֖ל כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

verses.restored: Jehoahaz sought favor of YHWH, and YHWH listened to him, for he saw oppression of Israel, because king of Aram oppressed them.

familiar.text: And Jehoahaz besought the LORD, and the LORD hearkened unto him: for he saw the oppression of Israel, because the king of Syria oppressed them.

modern.text: Then Jehoahaz sought the favor of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him because He saw the oppression that the king of Aram had inflicted on Israel.

original.text: וַיְחַ֥ל יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֤י רָאָה֙ אֶת לַ֣חַץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּֽי לָחַ֥ץ אֹתָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ אֲרָֽם

verses.restored: YHWH gave Israel a deliverer, and they went out from under hand of Aram; children of Israel lived in their tents as before.

familiar.text: (And the LORD gave Israel a saviour, so that they went out from under the hand of the Syrians: and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents, as beforetime.

modern.text: So the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped the power of the Arameans. Then the people of Israel lived in their own homes as they had before.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֤ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מוֹשִׁ֔יעַ וַיֵּ֣צְא֔וּ מִתַּ֖חַת יַד אֲרָ֑ם וַיֵּשְׁב֧וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּאָהֳלֵיהֶ֖ם כִּתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם

verses.restored: Nevertheless they did not turn from sins of house of Jeroboam, by which he caused Israel to sin, but walked in them; Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.

familiar.text: Nevertheless they departed not from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel sin, but walked therein: and there remained the grove also in Samaria.)

modern.text: Nevertheless, they did not turn away from the sins that the house of Jeroboam had caused Israel to commit, but they continued to walk in them. The Asherah pole even remained standing in Samaria.

original.text: אַ֠ךְ לֹֽא סָ֜רוּ מֵחַטֹּ֧אות בֵּית יָרָבְעָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר החטי אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣הּ הָלָ֑ךְ וְגַם֙ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה עָמְדָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: For he left to Jehoahaz from army only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, because king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like dust for threshing.

familiar.text: Neither did he leave of the people to Jehoahaz but fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen; for the king of Syria had destroyed them, and had made them like the dust by threshing.

modern.text: Jehoahaz had no army left, except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, because the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.

original.text: כִּ֣י לֹא֩ הִשְׁאִ֨יר לִיהוֹאָחָ֜ז עָ֗ם כִּ֣י אִם חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים פָּֽרָשִׁים֙ וַעֲשָׂ֣רָה רֶ֔כֶב וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים רַגְלִ֑י כִּ֤י אִבְּדָם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם וַיְשִׂמֵ֥ם כֶּֽעָפָ֖ר לָדֻֽשׁ

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Jehoahaz, all he did, and his might, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, along with all his accomplishments and his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֧י יְהוֹאָחָ֛ז וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וּגְבוּרָת֑וֹ הֲלוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Jehoahaz lay with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. Joash his son became king in his place.

familiar.text: And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers; and they buried him in Samaria: and Joash his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Jehoahaz rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. And his son Jehoash reigned in his place. Jehoash Reigns in Israel

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹאָחָז֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: In thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned sixteen years.

familiar.text: In the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah began Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned sixteen years.

modern.text: In the thirty-seventh year of the reign of Joash over Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָ֨שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֤ז עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH; he did not turn from all sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, but walked in them.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD; he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin: but he walked therein.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not turn away from all the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit, but he walked in them.

original.text: וַיַּֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מִכָּל חַטֹּ֞אות יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּן נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֥הּ הָלָֽךְ

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Joash, all he did, and his might by which he fought Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel?

familiar.text: And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might wherewith he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoash, along with all his accomplishments and his might, including his war against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י יוֹאָשׁ֙ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וּגְב֣וּרָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִלְחַ֔ם עִ֖ם אֲמַצְיָ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Joash lay with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with kings of Israel.

familiar.text: And Joash slept with his fathers; and Jeroboam sat upon his throne: and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

modern.text: And Jehoash rested with his fathers, and Jeroboam succeeded him on the throne. Jehoash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. Elisha’s Final Prophecy

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹאָשׁ֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וְיָרָבְעָ֖ם יָשַׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְא֑וֹ וַיִּקָּבֵ֤ר יוֹאָשׁ֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן עִ֖ם מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Elisha became sick with sickness from which he died. Joash king of Israel came down to him, wept over his face, and said, My father, my father, chariot of Israel and its horsemen!

familiar.text: Now Elisha was fallen sick of his sickness whereof he died. And Joash the king of Israel came down unto him, and wept over his face, and said, O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.

modern.text: When Elisha had fallen sick with the illness from which he would die, Jehoash king of Israel came down to him and wept over him, saying, “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!”

original.text: וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה אֶת חָלְי֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָמ֖וּת בּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨רֶד אֵלָ֜יו יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֵּ֤בְךְּ עַל פָּנָיו֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָבִ֣י אָבִ֔י רֶ֥כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּפָרָשָֽׁיו

verses.restored: Elisha said to him, Take bow and arrows. He took bow and arrows.

familiar.text: And Elisha said unto him, Take bow and arrows. And he took unto him bow and arrows.

modern.text: Elisha told him, “Take a bow and some arrows.” So Jehoash took a bow and some arrows.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע קַ֖ח קֶ֣שֶׁת וְחִצִּ֑ים וַיִּקַּ֥ח אֵלָ֖יו קֶ֥שֶׁת וְחִצִּֽים

verses.restored: He said to king of Israel, Put your hand upon bow. He put his hand, and Elisha placed his hands upon king's hands.

familiar.text: And he said to the king of Israel, Put thine hand upon the bow. And he put his hand upon it: and Elisha put his hands upon the king’s hands.

modern.text: Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow.” So the king put his hand on the bow, and Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַרְכֵּ֤ב יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל הַקֶּ֔שֶׁת וַיַּרְכֵּ֖ב יָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֧שֶׂם אֱלִישָׁ֛ע יָדָ֖יו עַל יְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: He said, Open window eastward. He opened it. Elisha said, Shoot. He shot. He said, Arrow of deliverance of YHWH, arrow of deliverance against Aram; you shall strike Aram at Aphek until finishing.

familiar.text: And he said, Open the window eastward. And he opened it. Then Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, The arrow of the LORD’s deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance from Syria: for thou shalt smite the Syrians in Aphek, till thou have consumed them.

modern.text: “Open the east window,” said Elisha. So he opened it and Elisha said, “Shoot!” So he shot. And Elisha declared: “This is the LORD’s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram, for you shall strike the Arameans in Aphek until you have put an end to them.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּתַ֧ח הַחַלּ֛וֹן קֵ֖דְמָה וַיִּפְתָּ֑ח וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֤ע יְרֵה֙ וַיּ֔וֹר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חֵץ תְּשׁוּעָ֤ה לַֽיהוָה֙ וְחֵ֣ץ תְּשׁוּעָ֣ה בַֽאֲרָ֔ם וְהִכִּיתָ֧ אֶת אֲרָ֛ם בַּאֲפֵ֖ק עַד כַּלֵּֽה

verses.restored: He said, Take arrows. He took them. He said to king of Israel, Strike ground. He struck three times and stopped.

familiar.text: And he said, Take the arrows. And he took them. And he said unto the king of Israel, Smite upon the ground. And he smote thrice, and stayed.

modern.text: Then Elisha said, “Take the arrows!” So he took them, and Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground!” So he struck the ground three times and stopped.

original.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר קַ֥ח הַחִצִּ֖ים וַיִּקָּ֑ח וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לְמֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַךְ אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּ֥ךְ שָֽׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽד

verses.restored: Man of Divine became angry with him and said, You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck Aram until finishing it. Now three times you shall strike Aram.

familiar.text: And the man of God was wroth with him, and said, Thou shouldest have smitten five or six times; then hadst thou smitten Syria till thou hadst consumed it: whereas now thou shalt smite Syria but thrice.

modern.text: But the man of God was angry with him and said, “You should have struck the ground five or six times. Then you would have struck down Aram until you had put an end to it. But now you will strike down Aram only three times.”

original.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֨ף עָלָ֜יו אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְהַכּ֨וֹת חָמֵ֤שׁ אוֹ שֵׁשׁ֙ פְּעָמִ֔ים אָ֛ז הִכִּ֥יתָ אֶת אֲרָ֖ם עַד כַּלֵּ֑ה וְעַתָּ֕ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים תַּכֶּ֥ה אֶת אֲרָֽם

verses.restored: Elisha died, and they buried him. Bands of Moab entered land at coming of year.

familiar.text: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the bands of the Moabites invaded the land at the coming in of the year.

modern.text: And Elisha died and was buried. Now the Moabite raiders used to come into the land every spring.

original.text: וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִישָׁ֖ע וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֑הוּ וּגְדוּדֵ֥י מוֹאָ֛ב יָבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ בָּ֥א שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: As men were burying a man, look, they saw a band and threw man into grave of Elisha. When man touched bones of Elisha, he lived and stood upon his feet.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.

modern.text: Once, as the Israelites were burying a man, suddenly they saw a band of raiders, so they threw the man’s body into Elisha’s tomb. And as soon as his body touched the bones of Elisha, the man was revived and stood up on his feet.

original.text: וַיְהִ֞י הֵ֣ם קֹבְרִ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ וְהִנֵּה֙ רָא֣וּ אֶֽת הַגְּד֔וּד וַיַּשְׁלִ֥יכוּ אֶת הָאִ֖ישׁ בְּקֶ֣בֶר אֱלִישָׁ֑ע וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ וַיִּגַּ֤ע הָאִישׁ֙ בְּעַצְמ֣וֹת אֱלִישָׁ֔ע וַיְחִ֖י וַיָּ֥קָם עַל רַגְלָֽיו

verses.restored: Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all days of Jehoahaz.

familiar.text: But Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

modern.text: And Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel throughout the reign of Jehoahaz.

original.text: וַֽחֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם לָחַ֖ץ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹאָחָֽז

verses.restored: YHWH was gracious to them, had compassion on them, and turned toward them because of covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; he was unwilling to destroy them or cast them from his presence until now.

familiar.text: And the LORD was gracious unto them, and had compassion on them, and had respect unto them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, neither cast he them from his presence as yet.

modern.text: But the LORD was gracious to Israel and had compassion on them, and He turned toward them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And to this day, the LORD has been unwilling to destroy them or cast them from His presence.

original.text: וַיָּחָן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֹתָ֤ם וַֽיְרַחֲמֵם֙ וַיִּ֣פֶן אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם לְמַ֣עַן בְּרִית֔וֹ אֶת אַבְרָהָ֖ם יִצְחָ֣ק וְיַֽעֲקֹ֑ב וְלֹ֤א אָבָה֙ הַשְׁחִיתָ֔ם וְלֹֽא הִשְׁלִיכָ֥ם מֵֽעַל פָּנָ֖יו עַד עָֽתָּה

verses.restored: Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-hadad his son became king in his place.

familiar.text: So Hazael king of Syria died; and Benhadad his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיָּ֖מָת חֲזָאֵ֣ל מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ בֶּן הֲדַ֥ד בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz returned and took from hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael cities he had taken in war from hand of Jehoahaz his father. Three times Joash struck him and recovered cities of Israel.

familiar.text: And Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took again out of the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael the cities, which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Three times did Joash beat him, and recovered the cities of Israel.

modern.text: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that Hazael had taken in battle from his father Jehoahaz. Jehoash defeated Ben-hadad three times, and so recovered the cities of Israel.

original.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֗ז וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת הֶֽעָרִים֙ מִיַּד֙ בֶּן הֲדַ֣ד בֶּן חֲזָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקַ֗ח מִיַּ֛ד יְהוֹאָחָ֥ז אָבִ֖יו בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הִכָּ֣הוּ יוֹאָ֔שׁ וַיָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת עָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

translation_notes: Aramean oppression and destruction are described through royal theology, but civilians and ordinary soldiers bear the material devastation. No modern Syrian or Aramean community may be treated as an inherited enemy.
The unnamed 'deliverer' is not securely identified in the chapter. The ambiguity should remain rather than being forced into a preferred hero.
Elisha dies from illness. Prophetic stature does not guarantee cure, longevity, immunity, or spiritual failure-free health.
Joash's grief at Elisha's bedside is genuine within the narrative even though the king receives a negative royal evaluation.
The arrow ritual is symbolic and context-bound. It is not a divination or warfare technique for modern imitation.
Elisha becomes angry because Joash stops after three strikes, yet the instruction did not specify a number. This scene warns against leaders punishing others for unspoken expectations.
The promise to 'finish' Aram is violent war language and may not authorize extermination, genocide, or treating total destruction as faithful zeal.
The revival at Elisha's grave is an extraordinary narrative event, not a safe relic, corpse-contact, or resurrection procedure.
Touching bones does not establish that remains carry controllable spiritual power, and no bereaved family should be pressured to expect a miracle.
Covenant compassion interrupts destruction, while the military recovery remains partial and costly rather than a triumphal end to war.
safety_note: Do not stigmatize fatal illness, teach symbolic arrow or grave-contact techniques, punish people for failing hidden expectations, or turn Aram into a timeless enemy. Preserve Elisha's mortality, Joash's grief, the ambiguity of the deliverer, and the difference between covenant compassion and violent military victory.
